tagline: Out of the creosote and up where the snow sits.
intro: Lee Canyon Road leaves US 95 and climbs into the Spring Mountains. Deer Creek Road crosses over to Kyle Canyon, and Kyle Canyon Road comes back down toward Las Vegas, losing 3,000 feet in 20 miles while the trees thin out and the winter snow cover gives up.

The mountains rise out of creosote bush and Mojave yucca, with ponderosa pine and white fir on the slopes and bristlecone pine on the high ridges. Over all of it stands Charleston Peak, Nuvagantu in Southern Paiute, which means where snow sits. Up in the village of Mount Charleston, at about 7,500 feet, the mean high runs some 20 degrees cooler than in Las Vegas.

moments.title: Lee Canyon
moments.text: A small community 8,510 feet up the canyon, with a forestry fire station, a bristlecone trail loop and campgrounds named Dolomite and Old Mill.

moments.title: Spring Mountains Visitor Gateway
moments.text: On ground reclaimed from a golf course, the Seven Stones Plaza honors the Nuwuvi, and a telescope on the Pack Rat Trail picks out the 1955 crash site on Charleston Peak.
